decision.trend: Research has been focused on developing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with enhanced properties such as strength, ductility, and resistance to radiation damage. Various processing techniques, including spark plasma sintering, laser powder bed fusion, and magnetron-sputtering deposition, have been explored to achieve these properties. The effects of chemical short-range order, grain size, and precipitation structures on the mechanical properties of HEAs have been investigated.
decision.unsolved: Despite the progress made, there is still a need to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in HEAs, particularly in eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs). Additionally, the radiation damage resistance of HEAs under extreme irradiation environments remains a challenge.
decision.why: The trend suggests that designing a hierarchical microstructure with coherent interfaces and controlled precipitation structures can lead to enhanced strength and ductility in HEAs. This approach has shown promise in recent studies, such as the use of high-pressure and high-temperature treatment to achieve a hierarchically patterned microstructure in EHEAs. Therefore, the next step would be to explore the design of hierarchical microstructures in HEAs to overcome the strength-ductility trade-off and improve radiation damage resistance.
